subject: R2 decreasing when adding additional predictors

messages.author: 234887487104942e
messages.subject: R2 decreasing when adding additional predictors
parts:
Hello,
I am fitting a model with a bi-factor measurement structure where Gfactor predicts one observed variable (DV):
The model looks like this:

model1 <- "
# definitions of latent variables
Gfactor =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5 + item6 + item7 + item8 + item9 + item10 
Sfactor1 =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5
Sfactor2 =~  item6 + item7 + item8 + item9 + item10

# regression with observed variable as dependent variable
DV ~ Gfactor 
"
The model is fitted with a "sem" function, and latent variables are defined as orthogonal

fit1 <-  sem(model1, data = dat, orthogonal = TRUE)

 Then I fitted a similar model but included "group-factors" (Sfactor1 + Sfactor2) as additional predictors of DV.
 
model2 <- "
# definitions of latent variables
Gfactor =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5 + item6 + item7 + item8 + item9 + item10 
Sfactor1 =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5
Sfactor2 =~  item6 + item7 + item8 + item9 + item10

# regression with observed variable as dependent variable
DV ~ Gfactor + Sfactor1 + Sfactor2
"

fit2<-  sem(model2, data = dat, orthogonal = TRUE)
 
Both models converged normally with good fit. However, model 2 explains less variance in DV than model 1, which does not make sense to me, since it includes two additional uncorrelated predictors of DV.
Can anyone explain this result?

Thank you

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: R2 decreasing when adding additional predictors
parts: Your first model makes the DV an exclusive indicator of the G factor (just like its other indicators) and forces it to be orthogonal to the S factors, while the second relaxes these restrictions. Does the first model fit well, or does it not? If it does not there may be bias in parameter estimates, which might induce a too-high R2.
